parameters.description: This will return any contacts whose email matches the specified string exactly or where contact.email is like the specified string. We add wildcards to the end of the string to determine likeness. Possible Values include the following: Any string. An example is "?filter[email]=test@test.com".
parameters.name: filter_email

parameters.description: This will return any contacts whose first name matches the specified string exactly or where contact.first_name is like the specified string. We add wildcards to the end of the string to determine likeness. Possible Values include the following: Any string. An example is "?filter[first_name]=testfirstname".
parameters.name: filter_first_name

parameters.description: This will return any contacts whose last name matches the specified string exactly or where contact.last_name is like the specified string. We add wildcards to the end of the string to determine likeness. Possible Values include the following: Any string. An example is "?filter[last_name]=testlastname".
parameters.name: filter_last_name

parameters.description: This will return any contacts who have an updated timestamp >= the specified value. Possible Values include the following: Unix Timestamp, YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. An example is "?filter[updated_at]=1584595231".
parameters.name: filter_updated_at

parameters.description: This will return contacts with source = specified string. Possible Values include the following: Any String. An example is "?filter[source][]=Open House".
parameters.name: filter_source

parameters.description: This will return contacts with system_source = specified string. Possible Values include the following: Any String. An example is "?filter[system_source][]=API".
parameters.name: filter_system_source

parameters.description: This will return contacts with leadtype = specified explicit Value(s). If you want to filter by multiple lead types, then you'll need to add another filter[leadtype][] param to the url string. Possible Values include the following: "buyer", "seller", "renter", "agent", "vendor". An example is.
parameters.name: filter_leadtype

parameters.description: Pass in a timestamp as the value in order to find contacts registered after that time. Possible Values include the following: Unix Timestamp. An example is "?filter[registered_after]=1581188318".
parameters.name: filter_registered_after

parameters.description: Pass in a timestamp as the value in order to find contacts registered before that time. Possible Values include the following: Unix Timestamp. An example is "?filter[registered_before]=1612810718".
parameters.name: filter_registered_before

parameters.description: Pass a status value to return only leads of that status. Possible Values (can be set as one of the following integers): "0" - New, "1" - Client, "2" - Closed, "3" - Sphere, "4" - Active, "5" - Contract, "7" - Prospect. An example is "?filter[status]=7".
parameters.name: filter_status

parameters.description: Filter leads assigned to the given agent id. Possible Values include the following: Any integer used as an agent id. An example is "?filter[assigned_agent_id]=123".
parameters.name: filter_assigned_agent_id

parameters.description: This will return contacts with specific hashtags. If you want to filter by multiple lead types, then you'll need to add another filter[hashtag][] param to the url string. An example is "?filter[hashtags][]=tag1&filter[hashtags][]=tag2".
parameters.name: filter_hashtags

parameters.description: This will return all archived leads when value set as "1". Possible Values (can be set as one of the following integers): "0" - don't include archived, "1" - include archived. An example is "?includeArchived=1".
parameters.name: include_archived

parameters.description: This will limit the number of results displayed in the returned data array. Possible Values include the following: Any integer. An example is "?limit=25".
parameters.name: limit
